steps: Draw two overlapping circles inside a rectangle
Fill in the intersection (A ∩ B) first
Subtract the intersection from each individual total to find 'only' regions
Calculate 'neither' = total − (A only + both + B only)
For conditional probability: P(A|B) = n(A∩B) / n(B)
method_card.title: Venn Diagrams & Conditional Probability
method_card.content:
Venn diagrams show overlapping sets. \(P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)\). The region outside both circles represents 'neither'.

Set notation: \(A \cap B\) = intersection (both), \(A \cup B\) = union (either), \(A'\) = complement (not A).

Conditional probability: \(P(A | B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}\) — the probability of A given B has occurred.

Fill from the intersection first, then subtract to find the 'only' regions, then the 'neither' region.
method_card.example:
40 students: 25 like football, 15 like tennis, 8 like both.

Football only: 17, Both: 8, Tennis only: 7, Neither: 8. P(football | tennis) = 8/15.

bronze.display: 50 students: 28 like maths, 22 like science, 10 like both. How many like neither?

misconceptions.message: Maths only: 18, Both: 10, Science only: 12. Total = 18+10+12 = 40. Neither = 50−40 = 10.

P(A) = 0.7, P(A ∩ B) = 0.3. Find P(A only) as a decimal.
60 students: 36 like English, 24 like History, 12 like both. Find P(neither) as a simplified fraction.

misconceptions.message: Eng only=24, Both=12, Hist only=12. Accounted=48. Neither = 60−48 = 12. P = 12/60 = 1/5.

bronze.display: A Venn diagram shows 30 students in set A and 8 in A ∩ B, out of 60 total. Find P(A) as a simplified fraction.

misconceptions.message: P(A) includes both A only AND A∩B = 30/60 = 1/2.

Are events A and B independent if P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.3, P(A ∩ B) = 0.12?

misconceptions.message: Independent if P(A)×P(B) = P(A∩B). 0.4 × 0.3 = 0.12 = P(A∩B). Yes, independent.
